As per the facts of the case on 11.03.2014, at about 06.20 AM , the petitioner alongwith his family members were going in a car, from his house to Sadar Bazar Delhi.

And when they reached at main road Deenpur, opposite Dispensary New Delhi, suddenly a car bearing No. DL1LE8126 being driven by its driver came at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and hit their car from right side.
As a result of which petitioner and other occupants of the car received injuries .
The petitioner was taken to R.T.R.M Hospital , New Delhi.
He has suffered simple injuries due to this accident.

2. The present application/claim petition has been filed contending that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving by (respondent no.3/ Driver) who was driving Vehicle No. DL 1LE8126.

The offending vehicle was owned by Sushil Bohra ( respondent no.1/owner) and was insured with M/S IFFCO MACT No. 113/16 Asha Ram vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 6 of 13 Tokio General Insurance Co Ltd (respondent no.2).

sentences.text: So this Tribunal while assessing the income of injured under Minimum Wages Act of unskilled labour, has assessed income of injured as Rs.8,086/ p.m.
The PW1 has deposed that due to accidental injuries her husband ( deceased) could not earn money for about six months.
But on perusal of MLC the injuries are in simple in nature.
There is no such injury on the person of injured which suggest the Tribunal that petitioner could have been prevented to do work for six month.
So seeing the nature of injuries on the person of injured/victim and his age, which may took considerable time to heal up.
So an amount of Rs.8,086/ ( ie 30 days minimum wages of unskilled labour ) is awarded to the petitioners for loss of earning.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim's car driver was at fault, in any way.
Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a car bearing No.DL1LE 8126 by respondent no. 3 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
Being injured, petitioner is well within his rights to claim MACT No. 113/16 Asha Ram vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 9 of 13 compensation through LRs/ representatives.
But after his death the compensation has to be restricted only to loss of estate.
The reliance is placed on the case titled as Joti Ram And Ors Vs Chaman Lal And Ors AIR 1985 P H 2.
The only submission of Ld Counsel for insurance company is that the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the MACT No. 113/16 Asha Ram vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 11 of 13 petitioner.
The respondent No.1 has examined himself and admitted the fact that insurance policy was found fake on verification by the IO.
There is nothing on record which suggest to this Tribunal that Sudhir Dahiya and Nidhi Dahiya in any way connected with IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd.
opennyai_summary.arguments: So this Tribunal while assessing the income of injured under Minimum Wages Act of unskilled labour, has assessed income of injured as Rs.8,086/ p.m.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Reliance is placed on ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd Vs Ashokan &
Ors C.M.A No. 275 of 2016 and CMP No.2312 of 2016 of Hon'ble Madras High Court and Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd Vs Arvind Dattatray Shindode, First Appeal N0. 55 of 2023 of Hon'ble Bombay High Court.
In the given circumstances, the respondent No.2, insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner of offending vehicle.
24. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondent No.1 and 3 by holding that petitioner is entitled for compensation from respondent 1 and 3.

Petition in hands is allowed.
Respondent no.1 and 3 are directed to pay Rs.19,086/ with interest @ 7.5% from the date of filing of petition i.e. 12.11.2014 till the date of compliance to the petitioner as compensation in this case, within 30 days from today.
Thereafter interest @ 12% p.a for delayed payment.
Amount of interim compensation (if any) be deducted from this amount.
The awarded amount shall remain as tax free.
26. Considering the facts and circumstances, the entire amount be released to the LRs of deceased petitioner alongwith cumulative interest thereon in equal proportion.
27. Respondent no.1 and 3 directed to deposit entire amount of compensation with this tribunal,
within 30 days from today, with advance notice to petitioner.
